Microsoft Reports $36.6bn Quarterly Profit Days After Announcing Major Buyout Offer

29 Oct 2026, 06:36 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Business Desk · Source: www.bbc.co.uk

Technology giant Microsoft has reported profits of more than $36.6bn (£27.5bn) for the three months leading up to the end of September. The financial results were published just days after the company announced workforce reduction plans affecting a significant portion of its employees.

Financial Performance and AI Investments

On Monday, the Windows developer confirmed plans to offer voluntary buyouts to approximately 60,000 workers. The cost-cutting measure coincides with the company's heavy financial commitment to artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, mirroring a broader trend across the technology sector where firms are pouring billions of dollars into AI capabilities despite ongoing questions regarding the return on investment.

Following the announcement and the subsequent financial report, Microsoft shares rose by nearly 2.9% in after-hours trading in New York on Wednesday. Investor scrutiny of major tech company earnings has intensified as stakeholders assess the long-term sustainability of soaring AI-related expenditures.

For the quarter, Microsoft reported revenue of $92.3bn, bolstered by strong performance and growth within its cloud computing division.

Leadership Statements

Commenting on the financial results, Microsoft Chairman and Chief Executive Satya Nadella highlighted the company's strategic direction.

"We are delivering greater capability, choice, control, and cost efficiency for customers across our entire stack," Nadella said in a statement. "By helping organisations build and own their own intelligence, and earning trust through agent safety and security, we are translating our innovation into growing adoption and real-world impact across every industry."

Practical Implications and Context

For industry observers and investors, the juxtaposition of multi-billion dollar profits and sweeping buyout offers underscores the ongoing restructuring within the technology sector as firms pivot resources toward generative AI and cloud infrastructure.

What is Confirmed:

  • Microsoft's quarterly profit exceeded $36.6bn for the period ending in September.
  • Quarterly revenue reached $92.3bn, driven by cloud computing growth.
  • The company announced voluntary buyout offers directed at roughly 60,000 workers.
  • Microsoft shares increased by approximately 2.9% in after-hours New York trading.

What Remains Unknown:

  • The exact final number of employees who will accept the voluntary buyout offers.
  • The long-term financial return on Microsoft's ongoing capital expenditures in AI infrastructure.
